Q: Excel VBA Custom Function giving "Reference Not Valid" Error A:

YESS!! It was hyperlinks that had somehow been assigned to the Shape. Once I right-clicked, selected "Remove Hyperlink", then the macro worked just fine.

Q: ImportError: cannot import name 'TFAutoModelForSeq2SeqLM' from 'transformers' A:

Documentation for the newest version 5.14.0 shows AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM without TF.

Version with TF works for me with 4.57.6 (the last 4.x.x) but it doesn't work with 5.0.0.

So it seems you use old code and you may have to use older transformers.
Or you may try to remove TF and use AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.

Maybe version TFAutoModelForSeq2SeqLM still exists somewhere in 5.x as submodule
but I didn't test it (yet).
In 4.57.6 it exists in transformers/models/auto/modeling_tf_auto.py

Q: Node.js error Module not found error in visual studio code A:

Move your file to parents folder than try to run it file. node_module and file which you what to run should be in same folder.

Q: User has denied the privileges to the code error during applet running A:

I guess your question is that you opted not to block the application, but you still run into the 'application blocked' exception. I am answering this because this is what I am facing now.

The browser context is different from Eclipse and the browser's java-plugin will block unsigned jars which try to perform trusted operations. You need to provide more details so that others can help you out here. Different platforms and browsers add to the confusion. Try to debug this problem using the appletviewer tool first - it will help in clearing the first line of issues.

Q: org.xmlGetting exception while parsing XML.sax.SAXParseException: The content of elements must consist of well-formed character data or markup A:

Your XML is invalid

row-->Parent-->Child-->Child 1

You cannot have space in XML element name. Your xml element name Child 1 is having a space.

XML elements name must follow these naming rules.....

  • Names can contain letters, numbers, and other characters
  • Names cannot start with a number or punctuation character
  • Names cannot start with the letters xml (or XML, or Xml, etc)
  • Names cannot contain spaces

Q: running pip install from python 2.7.5 A:

You probably should (re)install a new version of pip explicitly for the new Python version. On pip installation instructions page it says that

pip works with CPython versions 2.6, 2.7, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and also pypy.

While installing, be sure to use the newer version of Python instead of the old one.

Q: How to get the row average across multiple columns when some values are zero A:

I am assuming the question gives a wrong expected output as the average of the first record is (10 + 5 + 0) / 3 = 5 (3 values are non-null but OP has made a calculation where 2 values are considered non-null).

Then turning each record of Table1 into record sets to be aggregated with the usual functions gives a shorter query than the existing answers:

SELECT (SELECT avg(rec) FROM (VALUES(q1),(q2),(q3),(q4)) t(rec))
FROM Table1

Obviously, this works with sum, count and other aggregated functions, even if all 4 fields contain NULL on the same record, the only trick being to correctly write the (SELECT avg(rec) FROM ....) subquery to avoid a cardinality_violation error (code 21000).

If the first record was indeed expected to be averaged to 7.5, treating zeroes like NULL, then each field from the scalar subquery must be replaced by the expression (below for q1):

CASE q1 WHEN 0 THEN NULL ELSE q1 END

Q: How can I set the p-value y-positions based on the higher mean of the group, not the maximum? A:

You can nudge the bracket (and labels) like so:

## ... +
   stat_pvalue_manual( ## ...,
                       bracket.nudge.y = -5
                      ) +
## ...

Negative values nudge downwards, the value is given in y-scale units. You can supply a common value for all comparisons like above, or separate values like bracket.nudge.y = c(-6, -10, 5).
